### Season outlook as written in the guide (p. 86)

Having success at a program like Duke is more and more impressive with each passing season. Not only does the school have some stronger academic requirements than most in that part of the nation, players that come in and have success wind up wanting a bigger stage in the SEC, ACC, or elsewhere. For the third straight season, head coach Manny Diaz had to hit the transfer portal to find a QB, eventually going with San Jose State’s Walker Eget to replace Darian Mensah, who had a strong 34/6 TD/INT ratio last season. The Blue Devils return their 1,100-yard rusher, but lose their QB, top three pass- catchers, and Diaz has to mostly retool the defense with a handful of returnees, but only a couple of impact starters. Of course, while his old employer went to the National Championship Game out of the ACC, it is Diaz’s Duke team that is the reigning conference champs. Under 5.5 Portal poaching for these mid- tier, Power Four schools is hard to overcome annually and I can’t help but wonder if this is the season it hits hard. Duke is 18-9 with two nine-win seasons under Diaz, but the market’s position on Duke seems to say a lot. The schedule is a little tougher with Miami on the conference slate and the talent level of the program definitely seems to have dropped. Even before Diaz, Mike Elko and David Cutcliffe were overachieving in Durham, but the new college football landscape is a lot to overcome year in and year out. My projection, however, is for 5.94 wins.

## 26. Open Questions / Risks

The guide's *Three Burning Questions for the 2026 Season* *(p. 87)*, with the answers as written:

### Who does what Darian did?

Mensah was really good for Duke after transferring in from Tulane and now he’s leveled up again as the expected starting QB for, ironically, Miami. He completed over two-thirds of his passes and nearly passed for 4,000 yards while leading the conference in pass attempts, passing yards, and passing touchdowns. Eget played extensively with the Spartans and had over 5,500 yards, but only 30 TD against 19 INT. It might be up to redshirt freshman Dan Mahan, who got all the spring opportunities he could handle with Eget hurt. OC Jonathan Brewer saw his group improve by a full yard per play and 8.3 PPG in Year 2, but he’s mostly starting from scratch in Year 3.

### Should the show run through Sheppard?

Nate Sheppard ran for 1,132 yards and 11 TD with 5.7 yards per pop as a true freshman last season. Despite the loss of an NFL- caliber lineman in the April draft, the Blue Devils are still big and experienced up front. While Eget or Mahan have an intriguing transfer in Penn’s 1,000-yard WR Jared Richardson, their other two primary receivers for this season look like 5-foot-8 Jayden Moore and 5-foot-9 Javen Nicholas, a Charlotte transfer. While Duke’s offensive numbers improved, the defensive numbers got significantly worse in Diaz’s second year, so a ground-and-pound type of approach might be a good way to go at least early on, perhaps leading to some value on Unders.

### Can Manny find the manpower on defense?

As an offense, Duke had 6.2 YPP, 285 passing yards per game, and a 66.4% completion percentage. Opponents had 6.3 YPP, 277 passing yards per game, and a 67.2% completion rate. In other words, the Blue Devils were rather fortunate that Mensah played as well as he did and that the team finished +10 in TO margin. Duke was comfortably outgained on a per-play basis in ACC action. The Blue Devils also went from 43 sacks down to 26. Across the board, the defensive numbers were worse, including a 1.3-yard spike in YPP allowed that is hard to overlook given the offensive losses. With Diaz so accomplished on the defensive side, it’s time for that unit to step up.
